She calls it a great achievement and says he should let The Sporting News know. Crash shakes his head, saying the record would be a dubious honor. Annie argues it would be great and that he could break the all-time minor league home run record if he hits twenty more. Crash tells her no, asking her not to tell anyone. As the pitching machine delivers another pitch, Annie swings and misses. Crash steps in, takes the bat, and drills a line drive. A little league team arrives, and the kids recognize him. While signing autographs, Crash asks, "Your place or mine?"

description: Annie swings and misses another pitch, muttering under her breath. Crash steps in without a word, takes his stance, and drives the next pitch with a sharp crack of the bat. name: Crash Confronts Annie at the Batting Field
description: Annie stands at the plate, bat in hand, as the mechanical pitching machine delivers. She swings and misses, then declares she is committed to Nuke for the season. Crash responds by questioning her choice, calling Nuke a dim, pretty boy, and challenges her idea of commitment. Annie defends him, saying he’s inexperienced and her role is to guide him. Crash counters that her real issue is fear—fear of a real connection with someone like him. As he speaks, he steps up to the plate and hits three line drives, each timed with a pointed remark. He accuses her of hiding behind poetry and mysticism, of sabotaging anything real so she can play the tragic woman. The machine runs out of balls. Silence follows. Annie softens, saying, 'Oh Crash... you do make speeches.' Crash sets the bat down and walks toward the gate. Annie follows. A Little League team arrives, children in uniform with their coaches. One of the kids recognizes Crash and asks for an autograph. Crash stops to sign, surrounded by the group. As he signs, he looks over and says, 'Well, Annie, your place or mine?' Annie hesitates, then says, 'You got me all confused.' Crash replies, 'A batter has two tenths of a second to decide whether to swing.' Annie answers, 'I'm not a real batter. I'm a woman.' A young player interrupts, yelling, 'Hey, when are you guys gonna start winning? You're terrible!'
